Network

Dedicated server setup and two-client proof

Follow the installed5.8.3 source-build/toolchain route and record actual commands, not fictional logs.

On this page
PreparationLocal development runServer cookingAcceptance

Preparation

The public dedicated-server tutorial uses a C++ project and source engine build. Record your exact engine branch/changelist, SDK/compiler, platform and PaperZD version. Build the Editor target cleanly, then define the project dedicated-server target in the implementation repository according to the installed build rules. This guide does not emit Unreal target/source files or pretend an executable already exists.

Local development run

  1. Configure BP_ZoneGameMode with registered controller/pawn/state classes. L_NetworkLab has clear PlayerStarts, blocking terrain and one zone runtime.
  2. Launch one actual dedicated-server build on a chosen game port and two separate client processes. Use the actual executable/map argument produced by your build; record it in the test evidence.
  3. Use a private fixture authenticator in03; implement account/provider and durable admission boundaries04–05. The fixture is not production identity.
  4. Confirm server log has no local player/UI and each connection owns one controller/PlayerState/pawn. Inspect roles on both clients.
  5. Move, jump, sprint, dodge and swim; observe remote sprites without client-only animation state being treated as a replicated fact.
  6. Disconnect A; verify B remains and A reconnects under the documented session policy. Test malicious attempts to send server requests through a world Actor the client does not own.

Server cooking

Ensure required gameplay definitions/maps are cooked and server-only rules do not accidentally require UMG or a rendering component. Cosmetic assets may be absent/stripped on dedicated build; gameplay must continue. Client build must include active visual/UI content but no backend secrets or dev mutation fixtures.

Acceptance

The test passes only when two real clients move through actual 3D collision, server validation rejects invalid requests, remote state converges and reconnect produces one body. PIE configuration success alone is not packaged server proof.

Evidence and external references

External links need internet; the manual itself remains offline. Public documentation does not prove installed compatibility.

  • Setting up dedicated servers — Public 5.8 tutorial checked; its dedicated-server build route requires a C++ project and source engine build. No target built here.
  • Networking overview — Public 5.8 documentation checked; actor/RPC replication is not automatic replication of all game logic.
  • Networked Character Movement — Public 5.8 description checked: saved moves, server corrections and simulated proxy smoothing. Custom sprint/dodge integration still requires installed-source and runtime verification.

Planned game assets are not compiled assets. Values are proposals unless explicitly evidenced. Verification and limitations.
